text:
alex_infra: Heads-up — seeing repeated eth0 flap/drain cycles on a small set of g7a instances in us-west-2 over the last 30m. Affected ASG: gpu-renderer-usw2-prod. ~20 nodes showing RX/TX errors and RDMA connect failures.

alex_infra: quick snapshot:
```
$ sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_missed'
rx_errors: 1248
tx_errors: 632
rx_missed: 0
```

alex_infra: dmesg shows repeated: 
```
NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (ena): transmit queue 0 timed out
ena 0000:af:00.0: eth0: reset reason 3
```

sam_nic: @alex_infra thanks. Do you have the NIC firmware + driver versions?

alex_infra: firmware 2.1.7, ena driver 5.17.0-ena, kernel 6.1. Latest batch rolled 2d ago (small rollout).

sam_nic: hmm, 2.1.7 matches a rollout that had a retransmit timer tweak. We saw increased watchdog hits when jumbo MTU + GRO enabled on RDMA-heavy flows. Can you share MTU and tso/gro settings?

alex_infra: MTU 9000, GRO/TSO enabled by default. RDMA connections using RoCEv2.

lee_ops: We drained one node and repro'd with tcpdump + ibv_rc_pingpong — saw sporadic connection resets during heavy allgather shuffle. Dropping MTU to 1500 stopped the immediate flaps. Not sure if that's acceptable long-term.

sam_nic: that's a useful repro. Two immediate asks: 1) Try disabling GRO/TSO on a repro node and stress the workload; 2) collect full ethtool -k, ethtool -S and rdma diagnostics. If disabling GRO helps, we can file a driver FW regression.

alex_infra: will run both now and paste outputs.

alex_infra: ethtool -k eth0 snippet: 
```
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
large-receive-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
```

alex_infra: turned off GRO/TSO on one host and re-ran our shuffle. No flaps after 10m so far. Looks promising.

sam_nic: good signal. We'll open an internal bug for firmware/driver interaction with RoCE + jumbo frames. Can you capture a buglog and queue it with support? Include: ethtool -S, rdma dev show, dmesg, and the kernel's hangcheck stack.

alex_infra: opened INC-3192 and attached logs + repro steps. Marked priority: P2.

infra-oncall-bot: Reminder: draining 20 nodes in ASG gpu-renderer-usw2-prod will scale up replacements; auto-scaling might trigger capacity delta.

lee_ops: @dana_sre please watch cluster capacity — we drained 5 nodes so far, replacements in 6m. If the fix needs full rollout we should schedule a maintenance window or throttle drains.

dana_sre: watching. For now we won't blanket-reduce MTU across fleet. We'll apply workaround (disable GRO/TSO) via machine config to a canary group of 3 nodes and observe 24h.

sam_nic: also curious if increased host CPU due to software GRO will impact latency/cost — please watch host CPU over the canary. If perf/regressions acceptable we'll coordinate a firmware rollback with cloud provider or push a driver hotfix.

alex_infra: noted. I'll add CPU and p95 network latency to the canary dashboard.

sam_nic: thanks. If anyone sees similar symptoms in other regions tag this thread. For now: workaround = disable GRO/TSO on affected nodes, MTU fallback to 1500 if needed, file with vendor (INC-3192). :thumbsup:

lee_ops: I'll draft a short runbook for oncall: detection query, immediate mitigation, and escalation path.

alex_infra: appreciate it. I'll update INC-3192 with canary results later today.

infra-oncall-bot: Deploy bot: canary config applied to 3 nodes in ASG gpu-renderer-usw2-prod at 2026-03-18T18:52:36Z

alex_infra: thanks — closing loop here for now.
